rows: Crop-dependence claim
Species count, production volume, economic value, and calories separately
Pollinator-dependent crops are nutritionally/economically important even if cereals dominate calories
Pollination-syndrome claim
Flower color, scent, reward, shape, and visitor morphology
Syndromes are probabilistic pattern-recognition tools
Honey-bee claim
Managed Apis service vs wild-pollinator diversity
Honey bees are livestock; wild bees supply resilience and specialization
Buzz-pollination claim
Poricidal anthers and vibration behavior
Bumblebees and some solitary bees do it; honey bees generally do not
Decline claim
Region, taxon, metric, and monitoring method
Managed colony loss, wild range contraction, and biomass decline are different signals
Pesticide claim
Exposure route, dose, crop, timing, and landscape context
Lab effects do not automatically equal field population collapse
Conservation claim
Floral continuity, nesting substrate, pesticide reduction, and landscape connectivity
Insect hotels alone are not habitat restoration
Deceptive-pollination claim
Reward absence, mimicry target, and pollinator learning
Deception works only while encounter rates and alternatives keep the system viable
